races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: PLEASE DON'T GO sets the standard and gets the nod with this step up in trip promising to suit on breeding but she doesn't set the bar that high so strong market confidence behind Gosden stable newcomer Henrik Ibsen would put a slightly different slant on things. Last month's 1m course fourth Fastidyah should also have more to offer now moving up in trip.

runners.note: Foaled February 5. 100,000 gns Stradivarius colt. Dam, 6f winner, half-sister to useful 5f/6f winner Newsletter. Newcomer from a top stable.
20/1, last of 9 in novice at Salisbury (1m, good to soft) on debut 20 days ago. Up in trip. Significant improvement needed with blinkers quickly reached for.
Both outings here, leaving 7f debut behind when 3 lengths fifth of 8 over 1m (soft) 24 days ago. The further step up in trip promises to be in his favour.
In good hands but looked more one for the longer term when well-held fifth of 7 in novice at Salisbury (1m, good to soft) on debut 20 days ago. Up in trip.
14/1, showed a fair level of ability when third of 6 in maiden at Haydock (1m, good to firm) on debut 47 days ago. Up in trip. May do better.
Naval Crown colt who needed the experience on his Lingfield debut and showed a lot more when second of 12 at  Bath (1m, good to firm), challenging when hampered final 100 yds.

Ghaiyyath filly who has shaped quite well on all-weather at Kempton (7f) and Lingfield (1m; collared late) on her last 2 outings. Plenty of stamina in pedigree so today's longer trip should suit. Considered.
Cracksman filly who shaped with promise when fourth of 13 in 1m course novice (good to soft) on debut 25 days ago, staying on final 1f. Likely improver, particularly over this longer trip.

races.name: Happy Birthday Mark Holton Nursery
races.verdict: SON OF A FISH took his form up a notch when third on nursery debut at Leicester just over a fortnight ago and with better anticipated quickly returned up to 1m, Richard Hannon's colt gets the verdict. Similar comments apply to Astral Calling, so she could be the one to give the selection most to do, with Mick & David Easterby's pair Hope of Acklam and Diplomacy taken to fight out third.

runners.note: Showed a lot more second time up when narrow runner-up in a course seller (7f) last month and took another step forward when third of 9 in maiden at Musselburgh (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago. One to consider upped furth

Immediately shaped better switched to a nursery when third of 10 at Leicester (7f, good) just over a fortnight ago, going on encouragingly at the line. Has potential for better again returned to 1m so warrants considerab

Standout effort when third of 9 in maiden at Newcastle in June. Ran his worst race to date on nursery debut at Catterick (7f, good to firm) 9 weeks ago and has been freshened up since. Upped further in trip.
Standout effort when sixth of 12 in novice at Southwell (7f) in July. Likely to be seen in a better light now tackling a nursery for the first time upped to 1m.
Best effort in his qualifying runs when seventh of 11 in maiden at Beverley (5f, good) in May. Upped markedly in trip for his nursery debut/reappearance (has also been gelded).
Didn't show a great deal in 3 outings over 6f/7f in midsummer and failed to improve right away on nursery bow after 8 weeks off at Leicester (7f, good) recently. Upped to 1m but may need more time.
Little impact in 3 outings over 7f in recent weeks. May prove a different proposition now tackling a nursery over this longer trip.
Hasn't shown much to be positive about so far but this switch to a nursery over 1m could see him in a better light.

Benefited from the step up in trip as she showed improved form switched to a nursery when second of 7 at Musselburgh (1m, good to firm) last month. Nudged up 2 lb but every chance she will be in the shake-up.
Has shown little in her 4 starts to date, most recently when last of 10 on nursery debut at Beverley (7.5f, good) just under 6 weeks ago. Hopes pinned on first-time blinkers sparking improvement.

races.name: McSweeney Brothers Maiden Hurdle
races.verdict: LOVE ME TENDER may not have rewarded favourite backers in the Ebor last month, but Willie Mullins' German recruit shaped encouragingly and now with attentions quickly switched to hurdling, he gets the vote. Bud Fox is progressing gradually in this sphere and clearly with much more to come given his bumper form, he heads up the opposition, with Tyson Fury and Jules Winfield completing the shortlist

runners.note: Fairly useful Flat winner for Owen Burrows. Caught the eye on this qualifying run after 12 weeks off when third of 16 in maiden hurdle at Killarney (2m, good to soft) but looks the type to do better in handicaps.

Made a promising start in bumpers and has shown ability on all 3 starts over hurdles, most recently in a first-time hood when fourth of 14 in maiden at Kilbeggan (2m, good) just under 3 weeks ago (not given at all a hard

Ran as well as previously after 11 weeks off when second of 9 in novice hurdle at Downpatrick (2¼m, good) just over 3 weeks ago. Drop in trip almost certain not to suit so he looks opposable for win purposes.
Fairly useful on Flat up to 11f for Charlie Johnston. Little encouragement to glean from his 3 starts for current connections and handicaps after this likely more suitable.

Made a winning debut in a Ballinrobe bumper in April 2025 and took a step forward the following month when runner-up at Haydock. Ran too badly to be true when last seen in June that year and makes his hurdling debut afte
Pulled up sole outing in points and well held all 3 completed starts over hurdles (reported to have made a noise in running last time). Unlikely to be of interest until handicapping.
Well held both starts in recent weeks.
One-time fair Flat performer but out of sorts at present. Best watched on hurdling debut.

Fairly useful handicapper on Flat, again running well without quite proving strong enough in the finish to extend his run of in-frame efforts when fifth of 15 at Roscommon (1½m, good to soft) just over 3 weeks ago. Inter

For Fun gelding who showed nothing when tailed-off last of 6 in bumper at Punchestown (17f, heavy) back in February. Makes hurdling debut.
Showed a bit more tried in a hood when fifth of 12 in maiden hurdle at Wexford (17f, good) last month, though spoiled his chance by tending to jump right.

Sent off favourite and shaped encouragingly on his first outing since leaving Peter Schiergen (for €180,000) when tenth of 22 in the Ebor at York (1¾m, good to soft) last month, inexperience showing on just his fourth st

All his 3 runs so far have been short on promise and he makes minimal appeal this side of handicaps. Returns from 6 months off.

Notched up a second career success on what was just her second race at 2m+ at Gowran back in May 2025. Ran well when third at Navan (13f, good) the following month and hasn't been seen since. Makes hurdling debut.
Uninspiring Flat record but made a decent go of it on her first go over hurdles when third at Tramore (2m) last month. Went backwards from that at Wexford since so needs to quickly get back on track.
Sumbal filly. Dam pulled up sole start in points. Market check advised on debut. RESERVE.
Berkshire gelding. Dam (h99), 2½m hurdle winner, closely related to fair hurdler/fairly useful chaser (stayed 3m) Aviewtosea. RESERVE.
Wings of Eagles gelding who could hardly have shown any less on his completed start over hurdles. RESERVE.

races.name: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Classified Stakes
races.verdict: PLAID is building up a solid record and is preferred to fellow 3-y-o Runman in this useful classified stakes.

runners.note: Handicap winner in France last year but raced too keenly when tailed off in handicaps over 1¾m and 1½m at Ascot this summer. The return to 1¼m may help but arrives with a point to prove.
Dual winner in France who made a successful handicap/stable debut in Bahrain (1¼m) in December. Mostly respectable efforts back in Britain and likely to be on the premises here.

Ghaiyyath filly who was an easy winner of a 9f Hamilton handicap in May. Third in listed race back there in July and another good effort when fourth of 14 in handicap at last month's York Ebor meeting (10.3f, good to sof

races.name: Harvesting What Matters Most Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: CHICKER comfortably saw off a next-time-out winner on his hurdle debut in May and can make the most of the weight he receives from dual hurdle scorer Gambino. Jet of Stars is unbeaten in a point/bumper and could also play a leading role if the betting vibes are strong.

runners.note: Showed plenty when behind a fairly useful pair with experience on hurdling debut at Newbury in March. Made the most of a couple of good openings at Cartmel (17f) this summer but will likely need to pull out more if he's

Dual bumper winner who struck at the first time of asking over hurdles in 2½m Uttoxeter novice (good to soft) in May. That form was boosted when the runner-up won next time and he's open to progress back from a break.
Jet Away gelding who was bought for £230,000 after winning his sole outing in points. Landed short odds in a small-field Ayr bumper (heavy) in March and rates a very interesting recruit to hurdles.
Modest form at best in 2 bumpers last winter and best watched now hurdling after 7 months off.
Backed into 11/4 but folded quickly on Hexham bumper debut in April 2025. Pulled in 2 maiden hurdles over the winter and likely outsider on return. Tongue tied first time.
Offered something to work on when mid-field in Cork bumper for Gordon Elliott in July 2024 but not seen again until last of 4 in a C&D novice hurdle for this yard 16 days ago.
Fairly useful 1m winner on all-weather for Oliver Cole. Didn't get home when fifth of 9 on 17f Cartmel hurdle debut last month.
Fair maiden on the Flat in Ireland for Joseph O'Brien but no real promise on C&D hurdle debut for new yard in July.
Bumper winner but yet to better modest form over hurdles and given a break since pulling up (found to have sustained an overreach) over 2½m here 133 days ago.
Modest Flat winner who has largely struggled in that sphere this year and rates an outsider now making a rather belated switch to hurdles.

races.name: Weatherbys Stallion Book Nursery
races.verdict: FLOWER YOUMZAIN may well have opened her account but for better luck at Carlisle a fortnight ago and with further progress on the cards now tackling a nursery, Kevin Ryan's filly earns the vote. Wondervision seemed unsuited by the way the race developed at Doncaster recently and better judged on her penultimate success, she heads up the dangers. Empress Princess may prove best of the rest.

runners.note: Showed improved form to make a winning nursery debut at Wolverhampton last month, doing well to get up close home after meeting trouble. Seemed unsuited by the way the race developed at Doncaster (6.5f, good) earlier in

races.name: Seamus Mulvaney Bookmaker Novice Hurdle
races.verdict: BARTHOLOMEW progressed notably well in 3 juvenile hurdles for his current yard last season and is the clear pick at the weights, especially with a recent  Flat run under his belt. Columbus was tailed off in the face of a stiff task back on the level at York last time but there's better still to come from him as a hurdler and he's feared most.

runners.note: Lightly-raced point/bumper winner who impressed when opening his hurdles account at the third time of asking in maiden at Cork (17.3f) after 11 months off in July. Made the most of a good opportunity when following up at

Smart on Flat for Christophe Ferland. Joined Willie Mullins for €400,000 and confirmed hurdling debut promise when making all in a 17f maiden at Galway in August, jumping fluently. Tailed off in the Lonsdale Cup back on

races.name: Heineken Handicap
races.verdict: A further 2 lb ease in his mark might be enough to see STORM STAR land a first success on turf. Jimmy Speaking goes off the same mark as when narrowly denied at Yarmouth last week and is second choice ahead of Darkness, who has posted plenty of fine efforts at Goodwood.

runners.note: Very useful handicapper who has made the frame 4 times this year but needs to shrug off a lesser effort at Kempton 18 days ago.
Won a maiden at Killarney for Aidan O'Brien last spring and having been gelded, showed useful form for current yard in the UAE over the winter. Off 6 months ahead of this first start in Britain.

Shaped well when third in Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good) and Victoria Cup at Ascot (7f, good to firm) this spring but has ruined his chance with slow starts since. More than capable off this mark if breaking on terms bu

Losing run is mounting up but made the frame 3 times here this summer, including the Glorious meeting. Found his run of good form coming to a halt at Doncaster recently but his record here affords him respect.

Has recorded all 4 wins on all-weather at Newcastle but was a good second on turf at Ascot (1m, good to firm) in May. Creditable fifth of 17 in handicap at Doncaster (1m, good) 11 days ago. Eased another 2 lb and capable

races.name: Lord Mansfield Memorial Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: The normally-reliable FRONTIER PRINCE had a possible excuse in the Swinton and gets a narrow vote ahead of Letterston Lily and Patrick Neville's Dolly Dior. Dan Skelton handicap newcomer Hidden Fortune is another to consider in what looks a competitive race.

runners.note: Improved following a 17-month absence when sweeping to success over C&D (good) in April. Found 2m too sharp in the Summer Hurdle next time but resumed her progression back at 2½m when accounting for 7 rivals at Worcester

Won 3 times over hurdles in 2024/25 campaign but has drawn a blank since. Latest C&D fifth in first-time cheekpieces (retained) was respectable but he's no good thing to build on it.

Fair hurdle winner a couple of years ago but lost his way badly for Gordon Elliott and it remains to be seen whether a change of scenery helps to spark a revival.
Fairly useful handicap chase winner in January 2025 but pulled up on return from a year off at Carlisle in April and absent for a further 6 months since. Could only consider if backed.

races.name: British EBF Supports Racing To School Future Stayers Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: The pair with racecourse experience don't set a tall standard to aim at so the newcomers look the ones to focus on, GOLDEN SOUK getting the nod to make a winning start for a yard synonymous with 2-y-o success. The Can Can Man and El Waabil are another couple of debutants to note in a novice where the market will no doubt prove informative.

races.name: Brandon Hotel Handicap Hurdle (0-100)
races.verdict: ABORAS MAHLER has proved a different proposition in 2 starts this season, edged out only near the finish making handicap debut at Downpatrick, and he could still have more to offer now switched to Eric McNamara. He is the pick ahead of Lunar Landscape, who has been getting the hang of things over hurdles, with Glin Road Boy also of plenty of interest.

Hasn't made much impact in 3 maidens but offered a bit more encouragement when sixth of 20 at Cork (17f) in July. Open to improvement now handicapping, though bred to stay even further down the line.

Stepped up markedly on his comeback run earlier in the year when staying on strongly to win handicap at Limerick (2m) in April. Tailed off making chasing debut at the same course next time, but he could yet do better rev

Remains winless over hurdles but placed at Sligo and Clonmel on first 2 starts this season. Shaped as if still in good form at Ballinrobe on latest outing, still in touch when falling 2 out. RESERVE.

races.name: Virgin Bet Foundation Stakes (Listed)
races.verdict: NAQEEB is 3 lb better off with Boiling Point than when pipped by him in another C&D listed event in May and is taken to land this race for the second year in succession. Treble Tee should also have a say if his stamina holds stepping up to 1¼m.

Emphatic winner of a Newmarket listed race (1½m) last autumn but hasn't built on it since, including tailed-off last of 6 in Jockey Club Stakes at same course in May. Off 6 months.

Won this 12 months ago and short headed by Boiling Point  (who has to give him 3 lb now) in another C&D listed race in May (both good ground). Possibly unsuited by a much softer surface when well-held fifth in last month

Fairly useful filly who won a 1m maiden at Nottingham last August and has performed with credit in a pair of 1¼m handicaps since but has a lot to find on form at this level.

races.name: Bet With The Dewhurst Ring Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: A competitive handicap but MAGNOLIA has slipped to a lenient mark and with her yard going well she looks the way to go on her return from a break. Last year's winner Pure Gold seems primed for a big run and rates a big danger though, while in-form duo Follow Charlie and Annie Agnew can also play prominent roles.
